part2.intro: Three young people talk about their best day of the summer holidays.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Lily
texts.text: My best day was at the beach with my cousins. We built a huge sandcastle and swam in the sea all morning. Then my uncle made a barbecue, and we ate sausages and burgers on the sand. In the evening we played music and watched the sun go down. I didn't take my phone with me, so I haven't got any photos – but I'll never forget that day!

texts.label: B
texts.title: Duc
texts.text: I went to a music festival with my older brother. It was my first time! We stayed at the campsite there for two nights. It rained a lot and our tent got wet, but we didn't care. My favourite band played on Saturday night, and I danced for two hours. I bought a T-shirt with the band's name on it, and I wear it all the time now.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Martha
texts.text: My grandparents took me to a big museum in London. We saw dinosaurs and old cars, and I drew lots of pictures in my notebook. At lunchtime we had a picnic in the park next to the museum. The best part was in the museum café. There was a quiz, and Grandpa won it! The prize was a book about space, and he gave it to me.

items.q: Who slept outside?
Who got a present from a family member?
Who has no pictures of their best day?
Who spent the day by the sea?
Who had bad weather?
Who did some art during the day?
Who bought some clothes?

part3.title: Music in the park
part3.text:
Last summer, fourteen-year-old Zara Ahmed had an idea. "There are lots of young musicians in our town, but there's nowhere for them to play," she says. "So I decided to have a music festival in the park."

At first, it wasn't easy. Zara had to write to the town office to ask if she could use the park. "They said yes, but only if an adult helped me," she explains. "Luckily, my aunt works for a radio station, and she knows a lot about music events."

Zara put a message on the internet and asked bands to send her videos. Forty-two bands answered! "Choosing was really hard. I wanted everyone to play, but there was only time for twelve bands." The youngest musician was a nine-year-old boy who played the guitar and sang.

On the day of the festival, about eight hundred people came to the park. They brought blankets and picnics, and some families stayed all day. The festival was free, but Zara asked people to give some money for a new playground in the park. "We got over two thousand pounds!"

Did anything go wrong? "In the afternoon, it started to rain, and lots of people went home. I was really sad. But after half an hour the sun came out, and they all came back!"

Zara is already planning next year's festival. "This time I want to have dance groups and artists too."

items.q: Why did Zara decide to have a festival?
options: Young musicians had no place to play.
She wanted to play in a band.

items.q: Who helped Zara with the festival?
options: a family member who knew about music events

items.q: What was difficult for Zara?
What did Zara ask people at the festival to do?
options: give money for something in the park

items.q: What happened when it rained?
options: Many people left but came back later.

part4.title: Camping holidays
part4.text:
People have slept in tents for thousands of years, but camping as a hobby only {19} about 150 years ago. One of the first people to write about it was a British man called Thomas Hiram Holding. In 1908 he wrote a book that {20} people how to camp, and he also started one of the first camping clubs.

At first, camping was only popular with people who liked walking or riding bicycles. But when cars became cheaper in the 1950s, many families started to {21} their holidays at campsites. It was much cheaper than staying in a hotel.

Today camping is more popular than ever. Some campsites have swimming pools, shops and even restaurants. There is also a new kind of camping called 'glamping'. People {22} in big, comfortable tents with real beds and electricity – but it can be very {23}!

However, many campers still love the simple things: cooking on a fire, looking {24} the stars at night and waking up to the sound of birds.

We're having a barbecue in our garden {25} Saturday for my brother's birthday. Would you like to come? It starts at four o'clock. My dad is going to cook, and my brother's band is going {26} play some music. You don't need to bring anything, {27} you can bring your guitar if you like!
Ella

Hi Ella,
Thanks for inviting me! I'd love to come, but I'm going camping with my family this weekend. We're leaving {28} Friday evening and we won't be back {29} Sunday. I'm really sorry. Could we meet next week instead? Maybe we {30} have a picnic in the park.

part7.instruction: Look at the three pictures. Write the story shown in the pictures. Write 35 words or more.

pictures.caption: a family arriving at a campsite in a forest and putting up a tent
a storm at night; the wind is blowing the tent away
the family waking up in their car in the morning and laughing

part7.model: Last summer, Linh and her family went camping in the forest. They arrived in the afternoon and put up their tent near some trees. That night there was a terrible storm, and the wind blew their tent away! They had to sleep in the car. In the morning, they all laughed about it.

items.q: What will the family cook at the barbecue?

script.t: What shall we cook at the barbecue tonight? Burgers?
We had burgers last time. What about some fish?
Your brother doesn't eat fish. Let's get sausages – everyone likes those.
OK. I'll buy some on the way home from the beach.
Good. And can you get some bread too? We haven't got any.

items.q: Where are the friends going to meet?

script.t: Shall we meet at the bus stop and go to the beach together?
The bus is always late. I'll go on my bike. Let's meet at the beach café.
The café's closed on Mondays.
Oh, OK. Then let's meet in the car park next to the beach. I'll wait for you there at ten.

items.q: What time does the first band start?

script.t: When does the concert at the festival start? Seven o'clock?
The doors open at quarter past six, and the first band starts at quarter to seven.
And when's our favourite band on?
Not until quarter past seven. But I want to hear the first band too, so let's get there early.

items.q: What did the boy buy at the market?

script.t: Did you find anything good at the market, Tom?
I wanted some old CDs for Dad's CD player, but they were too expensive.
What about the paintings? There are always some nice ones.
I saw a nice one, but it was too big to carry. So I bought these comic books. Five for two pounds!

items.q: Which tent does the girl choose?

script.t: Hello. I need a tent for a school camping trip.
This big blue one is very popular.
It's too heavy for me to carry. What about the small green one?
That's only for one person. This orange one is for two people, and it's very light.
Perfect. My friend Ana can share it with me. I'll take it.

part2.intro: You will hear a man on the radio talking about a summer holiday club.
part2.title: Sandy Bay Holiday Club

script.t: Good morning! This is Radio Bay, and I've got some news for young people who get bored in the summer holidays. Sandy Bay Holiday Club is back! It's for children aged ten to fifteen. The club starts on Monday the twenty-second of July and it goes on for two weeks. Every day there's swimming in the sea and sailing, and this year there's something new: photography. You'll learn how to take great photos of the beach and the animals that live there. Last year we did painting, but not many people wanted to do it again. You don't need to bring a camera – we'll give you one. But please bring a hat, because it gets very hot on the beach. Lunch is a picnic on the beach, and that's in the price, so you don't need to bring any food or drinks. It costs fifteen pounds for one day, or twelve pounds a day if you come for the whole week. To book a place, phone Kelly Mabbott. That's M-A-B-B-O-T-T. Have a great summer!

part3.intro: You will hear Sophie talking to her friend Ryan about a party for their teacher.

items.q: Why are they having a party?
Where will the party be?
What will Ryan do at the party?
What present will they buy?
When will they get the classroom ready?

script.t: Ryan, have you heard? Mrs Collins is leaving at the end of term. She's going to live in Scotland.
I know. I'm really sad – she's the best teacher we've ever had. Shall we have a party for her on the last day?
Good idea! It can be a surprise. Her birthday's in December, so she won't guess.
Where can we have it? The school hall's nice and big.
There's a concert in the hall that day. What about the park? We could have a picnic.
It might rain. Let's just have it in our classroom. We can make it look nice.
OK. My sister's going to make a cake – she makes amazing ones. Can you play your guitar? Everyone loves it when you play.
Sure. I'll learn one of her favourite songs. And Max can take photos with his new camera.
Perfect. We should buy her a present too. Everyone can give a pound.
What about a book? She reads all the time.
She's got hundreds of books! She always talks about her garden. Let's get her a nice plant.
Good idea. A camera would be nice too, but it's too expensive.
When shall we get the classroom ready? On Friday morning, before school?
That's too early – the school doors don't open until eight. And Friday lunchtime is too late. Let's do it on Thursday after school.
OK. Thursday at half past three, then.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking to her friend about a book.
items.q: What does the girl think of the book?

script.t: Is that the book Mr Ali told us to read in the holidays?
Yes. I thought I wouldn't like it because it's got four hundred pages. But I couldn't stop reading! Every chapter ends with something surprising. I read it in three days.
Is the English hard?
No, it's quite easy, actually.

items.intro: You will hear a boy talking about a dance class.
items.q: Why did the boy join the dance class?
options: He wanted to do some exercise.
His friends were in the class.

script.t: Everyone asks me why I joined the street dance class. My sister goes to it, but she didn't ask me to come – she was really surprised when I arrived! And none of my friends dance. I just wanted to do some exercise in the holidays, because I sit at my computer too much and football has finished for the summer. And now I love it!

items.intro: You will hear a mother talking to her son about a holiday.
items.q: Where will the family go on holiday?

script.t: Dad wanted to go to the mountains again this year.
Oh no, all that walking! Can't we go to the beach?
Your sister doesn't like the beach – she gets too hot. So we've decided on Barcelona. There are beaches near the city, but we'll mostly visit museums and parks.
Great! I've always wanted to go there.

items.intro: You will hear a girl leaving a message for her friend.
items.q: Why is the girl calling?
options: to invite her friend to a party

script.t: Hi Kim, it's Lucy. You know the party at Sam's house on Saturday? I want to take some photos there, but my camera's broken. Could I borrow yours? I'll be really careful with it, I promise. I can come and get it on Friday after school. See you at the party! Thanks!

items.intro: You will hear a man talking about a new youth club.
items.q: Why is the man talking?
options: to tell people about a competition
to say the club is closing
to ask young people to become members

script.t: Our new youth club opened last month in the old library on Bridge Street. We've already got sixty members, but we want more! There's a music room with guitars and drums, a computer room, and an art room where you can paint and draw. It's open every evening from four until eight, and it's free. So come along and bring your friends – you can join on your first night!

part5.intro: You will hear Oscar talking to his mum about his first week at a holiday club. What did he do each day?

script.t: So, Oscar, how was your first week at the holiday club?
Brilliant, Mum! On Monday we were going to ride our bikes along the river, but it rained all day. So we went to the transport museum instead.
Oh, you love that place. What about Tuesday?
Tuesday was art day. We painted pictures of the sea. Mine's in my bag. I'll show you later.
Lovely. And Wednesday? Did you go dancing? The club's website said there was a dance class.
That's next week. On Wednesday the weather was good, so we did the bike ride that we missed on Monday. We cycled twenty kilometres!
Wow! You must be tired. And Thursday?
We were going to go swimming, but the pool was closed. So we had a big quiz in the hall instead. My team came second.
Well done! And today? Did you have the picnic?
No, that's next Friday. Today we learned how to put up tents in the field, and tonight we're camping there! I've only come home to get my sleeping bag.
